name: DaVinci Hero Still Shot Matching
use_when: Multiple shots in a scene need consistent exposure, contrast, color, and saturation.
A creative look makes shot differences more obvious.
The editor is second-guessing matches by comparing only adjacent shots.
avoid_when: The scene intentionally uses different color worlds or source types.
A shot is meant to feel disconnected, archival, fantasy, or phone-recorded.
The reference still is not representative of the intended scene look.

timeline_pattern.pattern: choose_hero_shot -> grab_still -> split_screen_compare -> match_clip_nodes -> apply_or_copy_grade -> review_scene
timeline_pattern.hero_rule: Choose a strong representative shot as the reference, then compare every related shot to it.
timeline_pattern.copy_rule: Copy grades only as a starting point; adjust each shot if exposure, camera, or lighting differs.
timeline_pattern.look_order_rule: If the creative look is extreme, build the look first, then match clip nodes under it.

motion.rule: No direct motion rule, but shot matching should preserve focal emphasis after zooms or reframes.

captions.rule: Do not let shot matching darken or saturate frames until captions lose contrast.

color.rule: Use stills, scopes, and clip nodes to match shots to a constant reference instead of drifting across the scene.

keyframe_values.review_rule: Look away or switch shots periodically because visual adaptation can hide color drift.
keyframe_values.good_enough_rule: If the match reads consistently in motion and protects faces/proof, move on instead of chasing invisible perfection.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render contact sheets against a chosen hero frame and compare histograms/scopes before applying per-clip filters.
implementation.remotion: Store heroFrameId and perClipCorrection deltas for scene matching.
implementation.blender: Use reference stills or compositor viewer comparisons when matching rendered and live-action plates.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use a representative frame as visual reference, copy adjustments, then refine each clip by eye and scopes if available.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Comparison View, Lumetri scopes, copy/paste Lumetri, and per-clip refinement.

common_mistakes: Matching each shot to the previous one and drifting away from the intended look.
Choosing a weak or unusual hero still as the reference.
Copying grades without checking each shot's lighting and camera differences.
Continuing to tweak after the scene already reads consistently.
qc: Is there a named hero still or reference shot?
Do all scene shots match that reference closely enough in motion?
Does the creative look amplify any remaining mismatch?
Are skin/proof/caption details protected in every matched shot?
Was the scene reviewed after looking away or switching context?
